newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end higher despite Olivetti slide.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end higher despite Olivetti slide.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Monday despite a collapse in the price of high-tech stock Olivetti which returned to the market after a two-day suspension only to see trading halted again when it went limit down.

The all-share Mibtel index finished 0.38 percent lower at 9,430 lire and the blue chip Mib30 also ended 0.38 percent down at 14,019. Trading volume was relatively thin with just under 400 billion lire worth of stocks traded.

Shares in food maker Parmalat also took a sharp knock, losing 5.43 percent to finish at 1,985 lire after health inspectors pulled 100,000 tubs of mascarpone cheese from stores over a botulism scare linked to the death of a boy.

Belgium said it too would pull the mascarpone -- a soft cheese used in desserts -- under the Giglio, Parmalat and Sol di Valle brand names -- while Sweden warned consumers not to eat those brands until more was known about the scare.

Olivetti grabbed the limelight, crashing 19.5 percent to close at an official 603.3 lire before the stock exchange ordered a suspension because the share price had hit a 20 percent limit on movements either way.
Dealers said Olivetti shares had traded at 600 lire and were being quoted at 580 lire without finding takers when the suspension was ordered.

The shares had last traded at 749.4 lire on Wednesday before stock market regulator Consob ordered a halt to trading for two trading days pending clarification of the company's first half results, which revealed a bigger than expected loss.

Brokers said the market was not satisfied with a statement by Olivetti on Friday in which the company stood by the figures. Olivetti's director general Renzo Francesconi resigned abruptly last week saying that the first-half statement did not fully reflect the state of the company.
